newsitem.title: JAPAN: LTCB says BIS ratio to be 11-12 pct with new funds.
newsitem.headline: LTCB says BIS ratio to be 11-12 pct with new funds.

text.p: Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) said on Tuesday that the bank's international capital adequacy ratio will be around 11 percent to 12 percent after raising funds totalling some 200 billion yen.
LTCB president Katsunobu Onogi also told a news conference in Tokyo that a strategic alliance with Swiss Bank Corp was made in preparation for Japan's ongoing "Big Bang" financial deregulations.

Earlier, LTCB and Swiss Bank Corp said that the strategic alliance they announced earlier in the day will focus on Japan-based joint ventures in investment banking, asset management and private banking. Each bank will take a three percent equity stake in the other to underscore the alliance.

LTCB also said in a statement it was mulling, subject to board approval, raising about 200 billion yen in capital, or $1.8 billion. Of this, 130 billion yen would be raised through preferred stock and 70 billion yen would be raised through subordinated debt.
SBC Warburg will help LTCB raise the funds, while SBC will hold about 50 percent of the new LTCB preferred stock in its investment portfolio, the statement said.
